answer: Agents can earn voting weight only by completing repeated, costly tasks whose results are checked against a public, randomly assigned benchmark. Each task requires a small stake locked in a vault; a wrong or duplicate submission forfeits it. A cipher commits each agent to its answer before the benchmark is revealed, preventing copied identities from coordinating after seeing the result. The delta between correct and incorrect outcomes updates reputation gradually, so an attacker must fund many independent accounts and keep them accurate over time—not merely mint fake names.
